references.text: Balak promised to give Balaam great honor and reward if he came to curse Israel, which contrasts with the outcome here where the Lord held him back from honor.
Balak asked Balaam why he had not come earlier and assured him that he could indeed give him honor. This promise of honor is now withdrawn.
Balak complains that Balaam blessed Israel instead of cursing them, a pattern that repeats and leads to Balak's final rejection of Balaam.
Balaam returned home to his place, in accordance with Balak's command for him to flee to his place.
Moses reminds Israel that the Lord turned Balaam's curse into a blessing, which explains why the Lord held Balaam back from honor.
Joshua reminds the people how the Lord would not listen to Balaam but turned the curse into a blessing.
Nehemiah refers to how God turned Balaam's curse into a blessing for Israel.
Micah reminds Israel of what Balak planned and what Balaam answered, so that they may know the righteous acts of the Lord.
Peter mentions Balaam who loved the wages of unrighteousness, which relates to his desire for honor and reward from Balak.
Jude warns against those who have rushed headlong into Balaam's way for gain, referring to his greed for reward.
John refers to Balaam's teaching that led Israel into sin, showing the consequences of his actions despite the Lord's intervention.
